Consider a mutual pair of recursive functions g() and h().

  1. int g(struct node *l) {
  2.     if (l == NULL || l->next == NULL) return 1;
  3.     if (l->value < l->next->value) return h(l->next);
  4.     else return 0;
  5. }
  6.  
  7. int h(struct node *l) {
  8.     if (l == NULL || l->next == NULL) return 1;
  9.     if (l->value > l->next->value) return g(l->next);
  10.     else return 0;

questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following function Merge() that takes the head of two linked lists.

  1. struct node {
  2.     int value;
  3.     struct node *next;
  4. };
  5. typedef struct node Node;
  6.  
  7. Node * Merge(Node * head1, Node * head2) {
  8.     if (head1 == NULL) return head2;
  9.     if (head2 == NULL) return head1;
  10.     Node * head = NULL;
  11.     if (head1 -> value < head2 -> value) {
  12.         head = head1;
  13.         head -> next = Merge(head1 -> next, head2);
  14.     }
  15.     else if (head1 -> value > head2 -> value) {
  16.         head = head2;
  17.         head -> next = Merge(head1, head2 -> next);
  18.     }
  19. return head;
  20. }

Assume that the input lists are correctly sorted. Which of the following are some of the possible behaviors when Merge() is executed with well-formed and valid inputs? Correctly merged linked list is merged sorted linked list.
